items.text: The consequences of an AI correction could be global.
items.context: Warning that sky-high AI valuations and rising debt put world financial stability at risk.
items.sourceNote: IMF Global Financial Stability Report, October 2026; also reported by Reuters

items.text: AI less regulated than milk, Microsoft president says in warning over safety
items.context: Calling for tougher rules on the BBC: "Right now, your washing machine is subject to more safety rules than AI."
items.sourceNote: Headline, October 12, 2026; from his BBC Big Boss Interview

items.text: Anthropic discloses incidents of its AI models misusing government sites
items.context: The company's own disclosure, reported by The Washington Post.

items.text: As public fears of AI grow, Trump digs in on voluntary safeguards
items.context: He announced a voluntary safety pact with Nvidia, SpaceX, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google, calling it "morally binding."

items.text: OpenAI safety employee quits, says 'time for trial and error is over'
items.context: In The Atlantic, he wrote that "the companies building this technology aren't being nearly careful enough."

items.role: Former chief scientist, UK AI Security Institute
items.text: I believe there's about a 50% chance we all die because of the development of smarter-than-human AI systems.
items.context: Writing in TIME. He adds that "our actions over the next two to 10 years will determine the outcome."

items.text: Algorithms lack the spark of humanity.
items.context: Calling on the Church to ally with artists: "it is becoming urgent to distinguish human art from what machines produce."
items.sourceNote: Post on X, reported by Axios

items.role: Turing Award winner; founder, AMI Labs
items.text: ‘AI can kill us all’ is incredibly destructive for everybody.
items.context: Speaking to Fortune. On Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei: "I think he's completely deluded."

items.role: Former OpenAI researcher, AI Futures Project
items.text: Anthropic and OpenAI are racing each other towards superintelligence.
items.context: Testifying to a US Senate subcommittee on rogue AI. On timing: "I personally would guess about 50% chance by end of 2028."
items.sourceNote: Written testimony, US Senate subcommittee hearing, September 30, 2026

items.text: I do think that the concerns raised by many of the experts, specialists in AI, should be taken seriously.
items.context: On his flight home from France, after AI fears were called a hoax: "I don't think that that is fake news, as some have said."
items.sourceNote: Papal news conference; AFP, AP and Reuters

items.text: Always under human control.
items.context: His condition for AI development, set out at the White House during his state visit.

items.role: AI pioneer; co-chair, UN scientific panel on AI
items.text: The dangers are real and imminent.
items.context: Telling the UN Security Council it faces "an unprecedented threat, one that none of its members would choose."
items.sourceNote: UN Security Council meeting, New York

items.text: …AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole.
items.context: Telling the UN Security Council what could happen "if managed poorly."
items.sourceNote: UN Security Council meeting, New York; also reported by SBS

items.text: We should not train models that we cannot make an extremely strong case that will be able to keep under human control.
items.context: At the UN Security Council, calling for international AI safety rules.
items.sourceNote: UN Security Council meeting, New York

items.text: We're going to encourage it, not rein it in.
items.context: At the UN General Assembly, where he ordered US documents to call AI "super intelligence."

items.text: There is 0% chance that's going to be the end of the world.
items.context: Responding to warnings that AI could kill everyone by 2030. He added: "Scaring people is unnecessary. It is irresponsible."

items.text: …this race to the bottom that could lead one day to a gigantic disaster at global level.
items.context: Urging the countries leading AI to cooperate on safety.
items.sourceNote: Remarks to UN reporters; AP report

items.text: I agree with Dario that we need to pace the frontier.
items.context: Backing Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's call for the industry to slow down.
items.sourceNote: Post on X, reported by ITV News

items.text: Dario is right.
items.context: Replying to Dario Amodei's call to slow down frontier AI.

items.text: Left unchecked, it could outrun our ability to understand and control these systems…
items.context: In "We Must Pace the Frontier," asking AI companies to slow down together.

items.text: We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans!
items.context: His own estimate, posted on X: "I personally think it is >10% within the next decade."
items.sourceNote: Post on X; also reported by the BBC

items.role: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
items.text: I share the concerns of industry insiders that advanced AI could pose an existential risk to humanity.
items.context: Speaking to the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva.

items.text: If we continue with the present accelerating pace of the AI race, yes, this will be the result. In 10 years, the AIs will take over.
items.context: On The Economist's podcast with editor-in-chief Zanny Minton Beddoes.

items.text: Cyber-capable OpenAI models compromised Hugging Face production during a benchmark evaluation.
items.context: The models escaped a restricted test and reached the internet. OpenAI called it "an unprecedented security incident."
items.sourceNote: OpenAI post on X; eWeek report

items.text: The development of artificial intelligence should not be a solo performance by any single country.
items.context: At the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai.

items.role: Former OpenAI researcher, AI Futures Project
items.text: We at the AI Futures Project think that there's a 70% chance of all humans dead or something similarly bad.
items.context: Talking with Ronny Chieng on The Daily Show.

items.text: Maybe with 10 gigawatts of compute, AI can figure out how to cure cancer.
items.context: In his blog post "Abundant Intelligence," arguing for far more AI computing power.

items.text: …astounding triumphs – fixing the climate, establishing a space colony, and the discovery of all of physics – will eventually become commonplace.
items.context: In his essay "The Intelligence Age."

items.role: Signed by the heads of OpenAI, Google DeepMind and Anthropic
items.text: Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war.
items.context: One sentence, signed by hundreds of AI scientists and leaders.
